brief: GS's Pasquariello notes the S&P's near-flat monthly returns since July (-0.13%, +2.62%, -0.45%, -0.93%) mask much larger swings in GS's own momentum basket GSPRHIMO over the same months (-30.19%, -13.67%, +26.96%, -18.60%), and that this week the S&P fell 57bps while the equal-weight SPW rose 80bps. His view: the primary bull trend stays intact but will deliver less upside, and sub-surface volatility persists, so he is not making a big bet right now. He ties this week's wear to Q3 hyperscaler earnings disappointing at the core even as capex guidance holds up, S&P earnings growth appearing to have peaked with estimate upgrades slowing, and a three-week selloff in mega-cap tech that included the index's 4th-largest stock's worst day ever as a public company. For the next two months he sees bulls holding a technical edge (downbeat sentiment, favorable seasonality, cleared positioning), while noting bears made the same argument in 2018. He also flags oil's midterm risk premium against a European equity rally (SMI at record highs), and endorses GS's existing tactical and structural bull case on commodities (BCOM +28% YTD).

cards.claim: The S&P 500 fell 57 basis points this week while the equal-weighted S&P 500 (SPW) rose roughly 80 basis points.

Goldman's flagship momentum basket GSPRHIMO returned -30.19% in July, -13.67% in August, +26.96% in September and -18.60% in October.
